experiment: #6 phase-split latency: Benign/Archimedean vs Adversarial/Logarithmic rows, on-device (Raspberry Pi 5, aarch64 A76).
setup: edge/src/bin/phase_latency.rs drives the real 3-thread pipeline (sensor->defense->rotation) with PhaseMixSensor alternating benign (small-magnitude -> epsilon_p<=gamma -> Archimedean) and adversarial (large aligned -> epsilon_p>gamma -> Logarithmic) segments. Phase determined in defense_thread from penetration_epsilon_windowed vs config.gamma. Latency tagged by phase (PhaseLatencySample) and summarized per phase. Uses MockModel so the measurement isolates the ROTATION-phase cost (budget_gated_rotation_fixed_basis), distinct from full end-to-end inference latency (see results/table_xi_latency.json). configs/edge_config.json gamma=0.292.
interpretation: Archimedean and Logarithmic phase latencies are identical at p50/p95/p99 (0.1029-0.1033 ms). The aggressive Logarithmic rotation imposes NO measurable per-inference latency overhead over benign operation -- as expected since rotation uses the identical budget_gated_rotation_fixed_basis path (phase only changes delta_theta magnitude, not cost). The single Logarithmic max (0.887 ms) is a tail scheduler-jitter outlier, not a phase cost. This supports the paper's latency-robustness claim: activating the adversarial (Logarithmic) phase does not degrade throughput/latency.
